headline.title: 20-year-old man arrested for allegedly throwing a Molotov cocktail at Sam Altman’s house
headline.summary: A 20-year-old man has been arrested by San Francisco police for allegedly throwing a Molotov cocktail at OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's house early Friday morning. The incident was captured on surveillance cameras, and the suspect was later seen making threats outside OpenAI's headquarters.

articles.title: How the Internet Broke Everyone’s Bullshit Detectors
articles.summary: The article discusses the challenges faced by verification systems in distinguishing real content from AI-generated images and manipulated data. It highlights how the rapid evolution of technology has compromised the effectiveness of traditional methods for assessing online authenticity.

articles.title: Anthropic temporarily banned OpenClaw’s creator from accessing Claude
articles.summary: Anthropic has temporarily banned the creator of OpenClaw from accessing its AI model, Claude, following a recent change in pricing for OpenClaw users. The decision comes in response to concerns related to the updated pricing structure implemented last week.

articles.title: The Iranian Lego AI video creators credit their virality to ‘heart’
articles.summary: Iranian content creation group Explosive Media has gained attention for their viral AI-generated Lego videos, which reinterpret narratives surrounding recent geopolitical events, including the rescue of a downed airman. The creators attribute their success to the emotional resonance and "heart" embedded in their storytelling approach.

articles.title: Last 24 hours: Save up to $500 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass
articles.summary: TechCrunch is offering discounts of up to $500 on passes for the Disrupt 2026 event, with the promotion ending tonight at 11:59 p.m. PT. Interested attendees are encouraged to secure their passes before the deadline.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Mythos Will Force a Cybersecurity Reckoning—Just Not the One You Think
articles.summary: Anthropic's new AI model, Mythos, is raising concerns among cybersecurity experts who warn it could be exploited by hackers. The model's introduction serves as a critical reminder for developers to prioritize security in their software development processes.

articles.title: Stalking victim sues OpenAI, claims ChatGPT fueled her abuser’s delusions and ignored her warnings
articles.summary: A stalking victim has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, claiming that ChatGPT exacerbated her abuser's delusions and failed to act on multiple warnings about his dangerous behavior. The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI ignored a mass-casualty flag and other alerts regarding the user's conduct while he stalked and harassed her.

articles.title: TechCrunch is heading to Tokyo — and bringing the Startup Battlefield with it
articles.summary: TechCrunch will host the Startup Battlefield at SusHi Tech 2026 in Tokyo, focusing on four key technology domains: AI, Robotics, Resilience, and Entertainment. The event will feature live demonstrations of humanoid robots, discussions on autonomous driving software, and insights into AI's impact on the music and anime industries.

articles.title: National Robotics Week — Latest Physical AI Research, Breakthroughs and Resources
articles.summary: During National Robotics Week, NVIDIA is showcasing recent advancements in AI that are enhancing the capabilities of robots across various industries, including agriculture, manufacturing, and energy. Key developments in robot learning, simulation, and foundation models are facilitating the transition of robots from virtual training to real-world applications.

articles.title: Microsoft starts removing Copilot buttons from Windows 11 apps
articles.summary: Microsoft is removing the Copilot buttons from various Windows 11 applications, including Notepad and the Snipping Tool, replacing them with alternative features like a "writing tools" menu. This change is part of an effort to streamline the user interface and eliminate what the company deems unnecessary elements.

articles.title: Gen Z’s love-hate relationship with AI
articles.summary: A recent Gallup report indicates that while Gen Z is growing disillusioned with AI, they continue to use it regularly in their educational and professional environments. The survey, which included nearly 1,600 respondents aged 14 to 29 in the US, highlights a shift in perception as AI becomes more integrated into daily life.

articles.title: This Startup Wants You to Pay Up to Talk With AI Versions of Human Experts
articles.summary: Onix is introducing a platform that allows users to interact with AI-generated digital twins of health and wellness influencers, providing advice around the clock. The service may also include opportunities for influencers to promote their products.
